heroText: Sofia is a layered Balkan capital where Roman ruins, Orthodox churches and mountain views sit inside a working city. Start at Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, follow the Serdica ruins through the centre, then plan a half-day to Boyana Church or Vitosha Mountain. Sofia Airport is metro-linked, making arrivals unusually easy.

areas.name: City Centre
areas.text: The central area around Serdica and Vitosha Boulevard is best for first stays, museums, restaurants and metro access.

areas.name: Oborishte
areas.text: Oborishte is leafy and central, close to Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, embassies and quieter boutique hotels.

areas.name: Lozenets
areas.text: Lozenets offers residential streets, business hotels and quick access toward South Park and Vitosha routes.

areas.name: Studentski Grad
areas.text: Studentski Grad is farther out but useful for budget stays, nightlife and access to university areas.

airports.name: Sofia Airport (SOF)
airports.text: Sofia Airport is east of the city and connects to the centre by metro, taxis and airport buses.

airportTransfer.value: 20-35 min by metro or taxi to central Sofia
airportTransfer.distance: about 10 km east of the centre

stayOverview: Use the City Centre for the easiest first Sofia stay, Oborishte for quieter culture-focused hotels, Lozenets for business and park access, or Studentski Grad for lower prices and nightlife outside the core.
hotelIntro: Sofia is practical by metro, so central hotels are not the only option. Still, first-time visitors usually do best near Serdica, Vitosha Boulevard or Oborishte for walkable food and sights.
rentalCars: Skip a car in Sofia; rent only for Rila Monastery, Plovdiv or mountain routes beyond the city.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay near Serdica or Vitosha Boulevard if you want restaurants, Roman ruins and metro lines close together.

travelTips.title: Airport metro
travelTips.text: The airport metro is straightforward, but taxis are useful for late arrivals or hotels away from stations.

travelTips.title: Mountain weather
travelTips.text: Vitosha can be much cooler than central Sofia, so take a layer even on warm city days.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Rila Monastery is the classic long day trip, while Boyana Church is easier for a shorter outing.

history.text: It became a municipium during the reign of Emperor Trajan (98–117).

history.label: 3rd century
history.text: In the 3rd century, it became the capital of Dacia Aureliana, and when Emperor Diocletian divided the province of Dacia Aureliana into Dacia Ripensis (at the banks of the Danube) and Dacia Mediterranea, Serdica.
In 339 BC Philip II of Macedon destroyed and ravaged the town for the first time.
The city was destroyed in the 447 invasion of the Huns and laid in ruins for a century.

history.label: 6th century
history.text: In 343 AD, the Council of Sardica was held in the city, in a church located where the current 6th century Church of Saint Sophia was later built.
Serdica became part of the First Bulgarian Empire during the reign of Khan Krum in 809, after a long siege.
It was once again incorporated into the restored Bulgarian Empire in 1194 at the time of Emperor Ivan Asen I and became a major administrative and cultural centre.
In 1530 Sofia became the capital of the Ottoman province (beylerbeylik) of Rumelia for about three centuries.

history.label: 18th century
history.text: Since the 18th century the beylerbeys of Rumelia often stayed in Bitola, which became the official capital of the province in 1826.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: Another neolithic settlement was founded in the 3rd–4th millennium BC near the site of the modern National Art Gallery, which has been the traditional centre of the city ever since.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It gradually became the most important Roman city of the region.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It grew into an important fortress and administrative centre under Krum's successor Khan Omurtag, who made it a centre of Sredets province (Sredetski komitat, Средецки комитат).

history.label: Regional role
history.text: It became the capital of the beylerbeylik of Rumelia (Rumelia Eyalet), the province that administered the Ottoman lands in Europe (the Balkans), one of the two together with the beylerbeylik of Anatolia.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Thus, Sofia became the first capital on the world to be overflown by enemy aircraft.
